problem: Classical robot navigation treats the environment geometrically, as accessible areas, or topologically, as graphs. It lacks the higher-level semantic abstraction (objects, places, concepts) needed for human-like reasoning in complex real-world environments, and the techniques for adding semantics were scattered across the literature.
motivation: Robotics is increasingly adopting behavioural mechanisms inspired by human psychology and thinking. Semantic knowledge allows a higher level of abstraction in how information is represented for navigation. A structured overview of how semantic information is acquired, represented and used in navigation is therefore needed to guide work on high-level navigation systems.
key_idea: Survey and organize the concepts, methods and techniques for bringing semantic information into robot navigation, spanning semantic knowledge acquisition (human-assisted vs. autonomous), knowledge representation (ontologies, cognitive maps, semantic maps) and their integration into 'semantic navigation'.
insight: The survey traces a progression from geometric navigators, to graph-theoretic/topological navigation, to semantic navigation. It argues that understanding the environment is a prerequisite for high-level navigation. It frames the semantic pipeline as environment modelling and semantic map building, plus learning new concepts, often through interaction with users. No experiments or ablations are reported (abstract only).
method: Taxonomy of semantic information acquisition: splits techniques into human-assisted (interaction with users to learn and label concepts) and autonomous acquisition.
Review of semantic knowledge representations: ontologies, cognitive maps and semantic maps.
Environment modelling and semantic map building: techniques for building maps that carry semantic labels and concepts.
Concept learning and knowledge representation: methods for learning new concepts and storing acquired knowledge.
Semantic navigation: integrates acquisition and representation into high-level navigation systems for complex real-world situations.

setting.observation: n/a (survey; covers various robot sensing setups)

results: This is a survey with no experimental results. It concludes that semantic information has moved robot navigation beyond purely geometric and graph-based approaches. It presents semantic navigation, which integrates semantic acquisition and representation, as the route to high-level navigation in complex real-world environments.
limitations: Survey only, with no quantitative benchmark comparison, as far as can be judged from the abstract.
Published in 2020, so it predates the large vision-language models and foundation-model-based semantic navigation methods (e.g., LLM/VLM-driven ObjectNav and VLN) that now dominate the field.
Focuses on classical robotics semantic mapping and ontology work rather than embodied-AI simulation benchmarks such as Habitat and R2R.
